privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: {brand} lets hosts collect photos, videos and messages from their guests. This page explains what personal data we handle and why. We are based in London, UK.

p: {brand} is operated from London, UK. The data controller is [COMPANY NAME] (TODO), company number [COMPANY NUMBER] (TODO), registered address [REGISTERED ADDRESS] (TODO), ICO registration number [ICO REGISTRATION NUMBER] (TODO).
Questions or requests: {email}.

list: Hosts: your email address, name, the details of the events you create, and payment records. Card details are handled by Stripe and never reach us.
Guests: the first name you type, and the photos, videos, voice messages and reactions you upload.
Enquiries: what you tell us when you contact us or use the partner form.
Technical data: IP address, device type and basic usage logs, used to keep the service secure and running.

sections.h: Why we use your data and our lawful bases
p: Under Article 6 of the UK GDPR we rely on the following lawful bases:
list: Contract (Article 6(1)(b)): to create and run events, store and show uploads to the people the host has chosen, send sign-in codes and receipts, and take payment.

Legitimate interests (Article 6(1)(f)): to keep the service secure, prevent abuse, fix problems and improve the service. For guests, this includes running the album you chose to take part in. We balance these interests against your rights.
Legal obligation (Article 6(1)(c)): to keep accounting and tax records and respond to lawful requests.
Consent (Article 6(1)(a)): only where we ask for it separately, and you can withdraw it at any time.

p: To help hosts review uploads, images may be sent to OpenAI's moderation service, which flags content that may be inappropriate, blurry or duplicated. It is used only for this purpose. No decision with a legal or similarly significant effect is made solely by automated means: the host decides what to keep, show or remove.

We use only essential cookies: a sign-in session for hosts, a language preference, and a per-event token that lets a guest's device keep its uploads together. We store only a hashed version of that token. These are strictly necessary to provide the service you ask for, so they are exempt from the consent requirement under PECR (the Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations). We do not use advertising, analytics or tracking cookies.
These providers process data on our behalf, only to run the service:
list: Vercel: hosting
Neon: database (London)
Vercel Blob: photo, video and audio storage (London)
Resend: email delivery
Stripe: payments
OpenAI: automated image moderation

p: Our database and media storage are in London. Some providers, for example for payments, email delivery or image moderation, may process limited data outside the UK. When that happens we only use providers covered by UK adequacy regulations, or we put safeguards in place such as the UK International Data Transfer Agreement (IDTA) or the UK Addendum to the EU standard contractual clauses.

list: Event photos, videos and messages: for the storage period of the host's plan ({freeStorage} on Free, {tekStorage} on One Day, {bigStorage} on Big Day), then deleted unless the host extends it. Hosts can delete an event or individual uploads at any time.
Account details: while your account is active, then deleted or anonymised on request.
Payment and invoice records: six years, for tax and accounting.
Enquiries: for as long as needed to deal with them.

p: Hosts are responsible for telling their guests that photos and videos will be collected and shared. If you appear in a photo and want it removed, ask the host first or email us.

Our service is not aimed at children. Photos of children may be uploaded by hosts and guests at family events; hosts and parents are responsible for sharing them appropriately, and we will remove content on request.
Under UK GDPR you have the right to:
list: access the personal data we hold about you
have inaccurate data corrected (rectification)
have your data deleted (erasure)
restrict how we use it
receive your data in a portable format
object to processing based on legitimate interests

sections.h: How to use your rights and complain
p: Email {email}. We will reply within one month, free of charge. We may need to confirm your identity, and for complex requests we may extend the time by up to two further months and will tell you why.

If you are unhappy with how we handle your data, you can complain to the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) at ico.org.uk or on 0303 123 1113. We would appreciate the chance to put things right first.
We may update this policy and will show the date above.
Email {email}.

terms.title: Terms
terms.intro: These terms apply when you use {brand} as a host or as a guest. By using the service you agree to them.

p: {brand} lets a host create an event page and QR code so guests can upload and view photos, videos and messages. Features depend on the host's plan.

list: You are responsible for the events you create and for who you share the link with.
You must have the right to collect the content and should let guests know it will be shared.
You are responsible for removing content that should not be there.

p: You may only upload content you have the right to share. Do not upload anything that is unlawful, abusive or infringes someone else's rights. You keep ownership of what you upload and give the host and us permission to store and display it as part of the event.
Do not misuse, attack or scrape the service, or upload malware. We may remove content or suspend events that break these terms.

Paid event plans are a one-off payment per event in pounds sterling, processed by Stripe. Plan limits and storage periods are shown on the pricing page. The Partner plan is a monthly subscription that renews each month until you cancel.

list: Money-back guarantee: you can ask for a full refund of any paid event plan within {days} days of purchase, no questions asked. Email {email} from the address on your account. Refunds are paid back to the original payment method through Stripe.

Your statutory cancellation right: under the Consumer Contracts (Information, Cancellation and Additional Charges) Regulations 2013 you normally have 14 days to cancel a digital service. By creating an event you ask us to start the service straight away. If the event has started or uploads have begun, that statutory right may be lost or reduced to a proportionate refund, but our money-back guarantee still applies within {days} days of purchase.
Partner plan: see "Partner plan" below.

p: We store event content for the period included in the host's plan. Download your album before that period ends. We cannot guarantee uninterrupted service, so keep your own copies of anything important.

The Partner plan is for businesses such as venues, planners, DJs and photographers, so the consumer cancellation rights above do not apply to it. It is billed monthly in advance and you can cancel at any time. Cancellation takes effect at the end of the current month, there is no refund for the current month, and access continues until then.
You must have the rights to any logos and content you upload, and you are responsible for telling your clients and their guests how photos will be collected and used.

We provide the service with reasonable care but on an as-is basis. To the extent the law allows, we are not liable for indirect losses, and our total liability is limited to the amount paid for the event concerned. Nothing in these terms limits liability that cannot be limited by law, including for death or personal injury caused by negligence or for fraud.
If you are a consumer, nothing in these terms affects your statutory rights under the Consumer Rights Act 2015, including that digital services must be provided with reasonable care and skill.
We may update these terms and will show the date above. If a change is significant, we will tell hosts with an active event by email.

These terms are governed by the laws of England and Wales, and the courts of England and Wales have jurisdiction, although if you live elsewhere in the UK you may also bring proceedings in your local courts.
